{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mt-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4237c169a292ad6eb78cad7521d2838e59b3d07f6cf1168e79c2b6bdef50d49f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mt-class-d:lineage:41","source_registry_sha256":"35425fc1b75886d4bce9129f5de9443ae8cee634cff4a62363bbcd7cc017fe32","source_liveness_sha256":"bf7b5d7e97593e3a1c6181f4785c9171cedac6e24ab65da907a644a4b4907add"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Communication and speed adjustment","heading":"C — Communication and speed adjustment","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Communication and speed adjustment

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Use headlights whenever seeing other road users becomes difficult, so they can see your vehicle too. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
If needed, briefly flash the headlights to alert another road user to your presence. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
When using windshield wipers in rain, snow or fog, turn the headlights on as well. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Turn the headlights on as daylight begins to fade. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
When driving requires lights, use headlights rather than parking lights. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
Use headlights when driving away from a rising or setting sun to help approaching drivers see you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
Use the horn when it can help prevent a collision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A01
Without immediate danger, use a light horn tap rather than a sharp blast. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A01
A light horn tap can warn a pedestrian or bicyclist who appears to be entering your travel lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A01
Use a light horn tap if a driver starts moving into your lane as you pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A01
A light horn tap can alert a driver who is inattentive or may not see you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A01
A light horn tap can announce your approach where a steep hill, sharp curve or narrow alley blocks the view ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A01
Give a sharp horn warning when a child or older person is about to enter the street on foot or by riding. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A01
Use a sharp horn warning if another vehicle is about to hit you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A01
If you lose control and are moving toward someone, use a sharp horn warning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A01
Do not sound the horn merely to pressure someone to go faster or move aside. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A01
Do not use the horn to point out another driver’s mistake or to greet a friend. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A01
Do not use the horn around visually impaired pedestrians. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A01
When a vehicle breaks down, use an available phone or two-way radio to notify authorities. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A01
If vehicle trouble requires stopping, move off the road and away from traffic whenever possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A01
Turn on emergency flashers when stopping for vehicle trouble. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A02
If a disabled vehicle cannot leave the roadway, stop where drivers can see it clearly rather than just beyond a hill or curve. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A02
Place appropriate emergency warnings behind a stopped vehicle to alert approaching traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A02
If no flares or warning devices are available, wave traffic around the vehicle from a safe place beside the road, using a white cloth if available. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A02
Never stand in a travel lane or attempt a tire change that would put you in one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A02
A raised hood or white cloth tied to an antenna, side mirror or door handle can signal an emergency. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A02
Avoid driving beside another vehicle and slightly behind it where its driver may not see you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A02
Speed up or fall back from another vehicle’s blind spot so its driver can see you more easily. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A02
When passing, move through the other driver’s blind spot as promptly as possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A02
Do not remain alongside a truck or bus because its large blind spots make your vehicle hard to see. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A02
Warn other drivers before changing direction or slowing so they have time to react. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A03
Signal before changing lanes, turning, merging, highway passing or parking. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A03
Signal a direction or lane change even when no other road user is visible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A03
Before a left turn, check traffic behind, signal and move close to the centerline well ahead of the turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A03
For a turn, signal for 100 feet in the city or 300 feet in rural areas while beginning to slow. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F36 | anchor: A03
Before turning left, look for oncoming traffic and yield to it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F37 | anchor: A03
While waiting to turn left, keep the wheels straight so a rear impact does not push you into oncoming traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F38 | anchor: A03
Enter the destination street just right of its center when turning left, without cutting the corner. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F39 | anchor: A03
After a left turn, move gradually to the middle of your lane and check that the signal is canceled. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F40 | anchor: A03
Prepare for a right turn by selecting the proper lane early and staying as close as practical to the right curb or roadway edge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F41 | anchor: A03
Complete a right turn near the right side without sweeping wide or crossing into the left lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F42 | anchor: A03
If a driveway, street or entrance lies before the intended turn, pass it before signaling so others do not mistake the turning location. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F43 | anchor: A03
If a vehicle is about to enter between you and the intended turn, wait until you pass it before signaling that turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F44 | anchor: A03
After a turn or lane change, cancel the signal manually if it has not canceled itself. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F45 | anchor: A03
Begin slowing as early as it is safe to do so. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F46 | anchor: A03
Before an unexpected stop or slowdown, tap the brake pedal quickly three or four times to warn following drivers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F47 | anchor: A03
Warn following traffic before slowing to leave a road without a separate turn or exit lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F48 | anchor: A03
Warn following drivers when parking or turning just before an intersection where they may expect you to continue. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F49 | anchor: A03
Warn following drivers before slowing for a hazard or stopped traffic they cannot see. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F50 | anchor: A03
Drivers must know basic hand signals even when their vehicle has turn and brake lights. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

Misconceptions: Parking lights do not substitute for headlights while driving; the appropriate warning and maneuver depend on the danger and road condition.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: be seen, signal clearly, adapt speed, preserve grip.
Glossary: Blind spot; emergency flashers; acceleration ramp; hydroplaning; skid; turnout; sight distance.
Dynamic facts: Posted limits, local rules and winter tire restrictions require current applicable controls; disputed numerical examples and the passing-speed conflict remain debt.
